- Actions (Patient): Monitor symptoms; increase fluid intake; seek further review if symptoms worsen or red flag signs develop; follow up with GP if needed
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Provided advice on management of probable GI infection; recommended GP review if no improvement or symptoms worsen

- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Fever, blood in stool or vomit, worsening abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, inability to keep fluids down, new symptoms
- Coping Strategies: Seek further medical review if symptoms escalate; reassurance regarding self-limited nature of illness

- Acute viral or bacterial gastroenteritis (food poisoning): High. Justification: Abrupt onset of diarrhoea, abdominal pain, vomiting, consistent with recent food/environmental change and absence of alarm features.
- Colorectal malignancy: Low. Justification: Family history present, but no red flag signs and acute time course make this unlikely for the current episode.
- Medication side effect (new inhaler): Low. Justification: Recent switch in inhaler, but inhalers rarely cause GI symptoms and physician notes this is unlikely.
